newsitem.title: UK: Smiths up, plays down Sextant talks.
newsitem.headline: Smiths up, plays down Sextant talks.

text.p: Shares in Smiths Industries Plc rose on Thursday, bouncing from Wednesday's decline amid positive press and analyst comment on the company's first-half results.
However the company played down a report in the Financial Times that it was in talks with French group Sextant Avionique aimed at securing a share of business on the Airbus programme.
A spokesman for Smiths said the company had had regular talks with Sextant over several years but had so far reached no specific conclusion.

"We have had talks regularly (with Sextant) about possibilities in the aerospace market," the spokesman said, "there are a number of issues we talk about but when any announcement is likely to be made I don't know."

The spokesman said Smiths already had "teaming" arrangements with companies such as U.S. avionics group Rockwell Collins and the talks with Sextant could be aimed at establishing a similar arrangement with the French group.
Smiths Industries shares were up 8-1/2p at 793-1/2 by 1127 GMT in modest trade of 925,350 shares, after on Wednesday dropping 10-1/2p.

Following Wednesday's results showing a 15 percent rise in pre-tax profit before one-off items to 80.2 million stg, the FT said the company had "strength in depth" and that prospects for European growth and a link with Sextant "promise further upside ahead."
Brokerages including Dresdner Kleinwort Benson and Panmure Gordon were positive on the stock today.
